Access Control Rules

Rules written onto the record itself and enforced by the backend, not by your app.

On the NodeGX backend a record you have no Read rule for is never returned by a query, and its changes are never delivered to you over realtime. It is a real permission boundary, not a display filter.

Backends that control access another way — Supabase, PostgREST, Directus, PocketBase — have no per-record ACL and ignore these rules. On those this port is disabled, with the reason on the row.

ports.name: date
ports.description: The instant of the last Read, for the other date nodes

ports.name: timestamp
ports.description: The same instant as milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC

ports.name: iso
ports.description: The same instant as an ISO-8601 string in UTC — the shape to put in a JSON body

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once the outputs hold the freshly-read instant

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation. This node has no other outcome — no Unchanged and no Failure — so it always fires together with Done, and wiring either one does the same thing. It is here on every action so that reaching for it is never a per-node decision

ports.name: input
ports.description: The instant to shift. A string or a millisecond timestamp arriving here is read as a date

ports.name: amount
ports.description: How much to add. Negative subtracts. Months and years use whole steps

ports.name: unit
ports.description: What Amount counts. Months and years are calendar steps and CLAMP: 31 January plus one month is 28 (or 29) February, never 2 March

ports.name: result
ports.description: Date shifted by Amount of Unit, or unset when Date could not be read

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires after Result has been recomputed, whichever input caused it

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when Date could not be read, leaving Result unset

ports.name: from
ports.description: The earlier instant, in the reading that makes Difference positive

ports.name: to
ports.description: The later instant. Difference is negative when this is actually earlier than From

ports.name: unit
ports.description: What Difference counts. Fixed units are exact and fractional (36 hours is 1.5 days); months and years are whole calendar steps

ports.name: absolute
ports.description: Drop the sign, so the output is a distance rather than a direction

ports.name: difference
ports.description: To minus From, counted in Unit. Unset while either date is missing or unreadable

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires after Difference has been recomputed

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when a date arrived that could not be read, leaving Difference unset

ports.name: a
ports.description: The instant being asked about

ports.name: b
ports.description: The instant it is compared against

ports.name: granularity
ports.description: How coarsely to compare. Day answers "is this the same day", which is almost always the question — two instants are hardly ever the same millisecond

ports.name: before
ports.description: True when Date is earlier than Compare To, at this Granularity

ports.name: after
ports.description: True when Date is later than Compare To, at this Granularity

ports.name: same
ports.description: True when the two land in the same Granularity bucket — the same day, month or year

ports.name: isBefore
ports.description: Fires after a comparison that came out Before

ports.name: isAfter
ports.description: Fires after a comparison that came out After

ports.name: isSame
ports.description: Fires after a comparison that came out Same

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when a date arrived that could not be read, leaving all three answers unset

ports.name: input
ports.description: The instant to take apart. A string or a millisecond timestamp here is read as a date

ports.name: year
ports.description: Four-digit year, in the host s local zone

ports.name: month
ports.description: Month as 1-12 — January is 1, not 0

ports.name: date
ports.description: Day of the month, 1-31

ports.name: hours
ports.description: Hour of the day, 0-23

ports.name: minutes
ports.description: Minutes past the hour, 0-59

ports.name: seconds
ports.description: Seconds past the minute, 0-59

ports.name: milliseconds
ports.description: Milliseconds past the second, 0-999

ports.name: dayOfWeek
ports.description: Day of the week as 0-6, Sunday first — JavaScript s own numbering

ports.name: dayName
ports.description: The English name of the weekday. For a localised name, format through Date To String

ports.name: isoWeek
ports.description: ISO-8601 week number, 1-53: weeks start on Monday and week 1 holds the first Thursday

ports.name: timestamp
ports.description: The instant as milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires after a new Date has been taken apart and every part output is up to date

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when a date arrived that could not be read, leaving every part unset

ports.name: text

ports.name: hasHeader

ports.name: delimiter
ports.description: The character between cells. Use ; for a European export, or a tab for TSV

ports.name: items
ports.description: The parsed rows — records when Has Header is ticked, arrays of cells when it is not. Every cell is a string, including columns that look numeric. Unchanged while the CSV cannot be parsed

ports.name: count
ports.description: How many rows the last successful parse produced, not counting the header row

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires once Items and Count hold the freshly parsed CSV

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the CSV could not be parsed, leaving Items and Count as they were

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the CSV could not be parsed, naming the line it gave up on; empty until a parse fails

ports.name: items
ports.description: The array to write. Records become rows; an array of arrays is written cell for cell

ports.name: columns
ports.description: Which properties to write, in order, comma separated. Leave it empty and every property found on the records is written, in the order they were first seen

ports.name: delimiter
ports.description: The character between cells. Any cell containing it is quoted automatically

ports.name: includeHeader
ports.description: Write the column names as the first row

ports.name: text
ports.description: The array as CSV text. Cells containing the delimiter, a quote or a newline are quoted and their quotes doubled, so this round-trips back through Parse CSV unchanged

ports.name: count
ports.description: How many data rows were written, not counting the header row

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires once CSV holds the freshly written text

ports.name: message

ports.name: level
ports.description: How loud this line is. In a cloud function the backend drops anything below its configured level, so Debug lines cost nothing in production unless someone turns them on

ports.name: data
ports.description: An optional object written alongside the message as structured fields. In a cloud function every property whose NAME says it holds a credential is redacted on the way out

ports.name: value
ports.description: Passed straight through to the Value output, so this node can sit inline on a wire

ports.name: log
ports.description: Writes the line. Nothing is written until this fires

ports.name: value
ports.description: Whatever arrived on the Value input, unchanged — this node never alters what passes through it

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once the line has been written

ports.description: Switches on, or fires Unchanged if it is already on

ports.name: off
ports.description: Switches off, or fires Unchanged if it is already off

ports.name: flip
ports.description: Switches to whichever state it is not currently in

ports.name: onFromStart
ports.description: State to start in, and setting it announces a switch on Switched even though nothing switched

ports.name: state
ports.description: True while the switch is on

ports.name: switched
ports.description: Fires on every state change, alongside whichever of Switched To On and Switched To Off applies

ports.name: switchedToOn
ports.description: Fires when the switch becomes on

ports.name: switchedToOff
ports.description: Fires when the switch becomes off

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the switch actually changed state

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when it was already in that state, so none of the Switched signals fired

ports.name: inputValue
ports.description: Number to remap, read against Input Minimum and Input Maximum

ports.name: minInputValue
ports.description: Value of Input Value that maps to Output Minimum

ports.name: maxInputValue
ports.description: Value of Input Value that maps to Output Maximum; set equal to Input Minimum and the result is pinned at Output Minimum for every input

ports.name: minOutputValue
ports.description: Result when Input Value is at Input Minimum

ports.name: maxOutputValue
ports.description: Result when Input Value is at Input Maximum

ports.name: clamp
ports.description: Holds the result inside the output range when Input Value falls outside the input range, instead of extrapolating

ports.name: remappedValue
ports.description: Input Value rescaled from the input range onto the output range

ports.name: filter
ports.description: Only errors whose Code starts with this text are reported; leave blank to catch every error in the app

ports.name: error
ports.description: Fires when an error passes the Filter, after every value output below has been updated to describe it

ports.name: message
ports.description: Human-readable account of what went wrong, safe to reword between releases — match on Code instead

ports.name: code
ports.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this kind of error, namespaced by node type, as in run-tasks/task-failed

ports.name: nodeId
ports.description: Graph id of the node that raised the error, or <runtime> when it was raised outside any node

ports.name: componentName
ports.description: Component the failing node sits in, or <runtime> when the error was raised outside any node

ports.name: nodeType
ports.description: Kind of node that raised the error, or <runtime> when it was raised outside any node

ports.name: errorObject
ports.description: The whole error event as one record, for logging it or sending it to an error-reporting service

ports.name: store

ports.name: email
ports.description: New email address for the signed-in user; leave blank to keep the current one

ports.name: username
ports.description: New username for the signed-in user; leave blank to keep the current one

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once the user record has been written

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the user record could not be written, after the reason has been reported on the error channel

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the last write failed; empty until one does

ports.name: runOnChange-user
ports.description: Whether a new value on User properties re-runs this node. On by default; untick to make this input passive so only the control signal runs it

ports.name: id
ports.description: Id of the signed-in user record; empty while nobody is signed in

ports.name: fetched
ports.description: Fires once the user record has been re-read and the outputs below are up to date

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires when a property of the signed-in user changes, including a change another node made

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when a Fetch finished and the outputs below are up to date

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: failure

ports.name: error

ports.name: username
ports.description: Username of the signed-in user; empty while nobody is signed in

ports.name: email
ports.description: Email address of the signed-in user; empty while nobody is signed in

ports.name: authenticated
ports.description: True while somebody is signed in on this device; a server render always sees false

ports.name: url
ports.description: Endpoint to connect to, which must start with ws:// or wss://; changing it reconnects to the new one

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.description: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal
ports.tooltip: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal.

ports.name: protocols
ports.description: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake.

ports.name: autoReconnect
ports.description: Retries after an unsolicited close with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the close as an error

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.description: First backoff delay in milliseconds; each further attempt doubles it up to Max Reconnect Delay
ports.tooltip: First backoff delay. Each further attempt doubles it, up to Max Reconnect Delay.

ports.name: maxReconnectDelay
ports.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many attempts there have been

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.description: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage; 0 disables retrying and a negative value means unlimited
ports.tooltip: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage. 0 disables retrying; a negative value means unlimited.

ports.name: jitter
ports.description: Spreads reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window, so a fleet does not return in lockstep
ports.tooltip: Spread reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window.

ports.name: heartbeatInterval
ports.description: Milliseconds between heartbeats while the socket is open; 0 disables it, and only enable it if your server expects the message
ports.tooltip: Send Heartbeat Message this often while open. 0 disables it. Only enable this if your server expects the message — it is application data, not a protocol ping frame.

ports.name: heartbeatMessage
ports.description: Application text sent as the heartbeat; it is not a protocol ping frame

ports.name: heartbeatReply
ports.description: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with; it is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and its absence is treated as a dead connection
ports.tooltip: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with. It is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and — if it stops arriving — treated as a dead connection. Leave empty to only send heartbeats.

ports.name: connect
ports.description: Opens the socket, replacing one already open without reporting a close

ports.name: disconnect
ports.description: Closes the socket and cancels any pending reconnect

ports.name: send
ports.description: Hands the current Message to the socket, or applies the When Disconnected policy

ports.name: message
ports.description: Value to send; objects are JSON-serialised, and ArrayBuffers and typed arrays go as binary frames
ports.tooltip: Value to send. Objects are JSON-serialized; ArrayBuffers and typed arrays are sent as binary frames.

ports.name: messageType
ports.description: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text; Binary encodes text and objects as UTF-8 first
ports.tooltip: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text. Binary forces text and objects to be UTF-8 encoded first.

ports.name: whenDisconnected
ports.description: What a Send does while the socket is not open: hold it in order, discard and count it, or also report an error
ports.tooltip: What a Send does while the connection is not open. Queue holds it (in order) until the socket reopens; Drop discards it and counts it; Report Error also sets Last Error and fires On Error.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.description: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted as dropped; 0 or less is unlimited and can grow during a long outage
ports.tooltip: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted in Dropped. 0 or less means unlimited, which can grow without bound during a long outage.

ports.name: connectionState
ports.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

ports.name: connected
ports.description: True only while the socket is open and messages can be sent without queueing

ports.name: retryCount
ports.description: Attempts made during the current outage; back to zero once the socket opens

ports.name: lastError
ports.description: What went wrong most recently, including why a reconnect was scheduled or abandoned

ports.name: queueSize
ports.description: Messages held because the socket was not open when Send ran

ports.name: droppedCount
ports.description: Messages that will never be sent, whether discarded by policy, by a full queue, or by the node being removed

ports.name: latency
ports.description: Round trip of the last heartbeat in milliseconds; 0 until one has been measured

ports.name: closeCode
ports.description: WebSocket close code from the last close, or 1006 when the socket died without one

ports.name: closeReason
ports.description: Reason the server gave for closing, which is often blank

ports.name: received
ports.description: The last message, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

ports.name: receivedRaw
ports.description: The last text message exactly as it arrived; blank for a binary frame

ports.name: receivedIsBinary
ports.description: True when the last message was a binary frame, in which case Received holds the buffer

ports.name: onOpen
ports.description: Fires every time the socket opens, including after a reconnect

ports.name: onMessage
ports.description: Fires once per message, after Received already holds it; heartbeat replies are not messages

ports.name: onMessageSent
ports.description: Fires when a message has been handed to the socket, including a queued one flushed on reopen; not for heartbeats

ports.name: onError
ports.description: Fires when something went wrong: a failed connect, a refused send, a dead heartbeat, or a give-up

ports.name: onClose
ports.description: Fires whenever the socket goes down, whether or not a reconnect is going to follow

ports.name: onReconnect
ports.description: Fires on every open after the first; a WebSocket cannot resume, so this is the cue to re-fetch rather than assume continuity

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose socket opened, a Send accepted for delivery (sent, or queued for the next open), or a Disconnect that closed something

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with nothing open, a Send discarded by the Drop policy, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the action could not be performed — no URL, a URL that is not ws:// or wss://, a connection that gave up, or a refused Send. Last Error carries the reason

ports.name: url
ports.description: Endpoint to stream from; changing it while connected reconnects to the new one

ports.name: transport
ports.description: How the stream is fetched: Fetch carries headers and a body, EventSource lets the browser handle reconnection, Auto prefers Fetch

ports.name: method
ports.description: HTTP method for the request; anything other than GET needs the Fetch transport

ports.name: headers
ports.description: Request headers as an object, for bearer tokens and the like; ignored by the EventSource transport, which cannot set them

ports.name: body
ports.description: Request body, sent as JSON unless it is already a string; ignored for GET and HEAD

ports.name: withCredentials
ports.description: Sends cookies and HTTP auth to a cross-origin endpoint, which the server must also allow

ports.name: eventTypes
ports.description: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to; only needed for the EventSource transport, as Fetch delivers every type
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to. Only needed for the EventSource transport, which delivers a named event only to a listener registered in advance; the Fetch transport delivers every event type.

ports.name: textPath
ports.description: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path such as choices.0.delta.content; leave blank for a stream of bare text
ports.tooltip: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path — for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, choices.0.delta.content. Leave blank for a stream that sends bare text. Whatever it names ends up on the Text output, which is always a string.

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.description: Opens the stream as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

ports.name: autoReconnect
ports.description: Retries after a failure with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the failure and stops

ports.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd

ports.tooltip: Reconnect when the server closes the stream cleanly. Off by default: an agent response stream is finite, and reconnecting would re-issue the request and start the response again.

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.description: First retry delay in milliseconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to Max Reconnect Delay
ports.tooltip: First retry delay. Doubles per consecutive failure, up to the maximum.

ports.name: maxReconnectDelay
ports.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many failures there have been

ports.name: maxRetries

ports.tooltip: 0 means keep retrying. Otherwise the connection reports an error after this many consecutive failures.

ports.name: disconnect

ports.name: lastError

ports.name: groups

ports.name: notFound

ports.name: completed

ports.name: flushSize

ports.tooltip: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered. 0 disables size-based flushing.

ports.name: add
ports.description: Buffers the current Data, flushing straight away if that reaches Flush Size

ports.name: flush

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Discards the buffer and resets both counters without flushing

ports.name: buffer
ports.description: Items waiting to be flushed, oldest first

ports.name: bufferSize

ports.name: flushedData

ports.name: flushCount

ports.name: droppedItems
ports.description: How many items Max Size has discarded from the front since the last Clear

ports.name: flushed
ports.description: Fires once Flushed Data holds a new batch, and not for a flush that found nothing

ports.name: overflowed
ports.description: Fires when Max Size has just discarded something

ports.name: cleared

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once an Add, Flush or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

ports.description: The shared secret the issuer signed with. Wire this from a Secret node
